prompt: What is a Git branch, as Git stores it?
hint: Look at what cat printed for refs/heads/main.

choices.text: A copy of the project's files
choices.why: Nothing is copied. Making a branch took no time and no space.

choices.text: A folder inside .git holding its own commits
choices.why: Commits are shared by every branch that leads to them; a branch holds none.

choices.text: A name for one commit
choices.why: Right. A file holding one commit's id.

choices.text: A list of the commits made on it
choices.why: It holds one id. The rest is found by following parents.

prompt: .git/HEAD contains ref: refs/heads/main. What does that tell you?
hint: HEAD names something, and that something names a commit.

choices.text: You are on the branch main
choices.why: Right. A commit now moves main.

choices.text: main is the only branch in the repository
choices.why: HEAD says which branch you are on, not how many exist.

choices.text: The newest commit was made by the owner of main
choices.why: Branches have no owners. HEAD names a branch, nothing more.

choices.text: main is protected from being deleted
choices.why: Being on it stops you deleting it, but that is a consequence, not what the file says.

prompt: main and opening-hours both point at 6555c9b. Ana is on opening-hours and commits. What happens to the two branches?
hint: A commit moves the branch HEAD names.

choices.text: Both move to the new commit, since they were identical
choices.why: Only the branch HEAD names moves. They were equal, not linked.

choices.text: opening-hours moves to the new commit; main stays
choices.why: Right. From now on they point at different commits.

choices.text: main moves, because it is the main branch
choices.why: main is an ordinary name. Nothing moves it unless HEAD names it.

choices.text: Neither moves until the work is merged
choices.why: The branch you are on moves with every commit. Merge is for bringing one into another.

prompt: A branch is a file of ___ bytes: forty characters of a commit id and a newline.
Ana switches from opening-hours back to main. What happens to index.html on disk?
hint: The working tree follows the branch.

choices.text: Nothing; files only change when you edit them
choices.why: switch is the one command that rewrites files as a side effect.

choices.text: It becomes main's version, without the Sunday line
choices.why: Right. Switch back and the line returns.

choices.text: It keeps both versions, one after the other
choices.why: Combining versions is what merge does, and switch does not merge.

choices.text: It is deleted until you switch back
choices.why: main has its own index.html, and that is what you get.

prompt: style.css has an uncommitted edit, and both branches have the same style.css. What happens when Ana switches branch?
hint: An uncommitted edit belongs to the working tree.

choices.text: Git refuses until she commits
choices.why: It only refuses when the switch would overwrite the edit, and here it would not.

choices.text: The edit is committed to the branch she leaves
choices.why: switch never commits anything.

choices.text: The edit comes with her
choices.why: Right. Git lists it on the switch so it is not missed.

choices.text: The edit is thrown away, since the new branch does not have it
choices.why: Git never throws away a change it has no copy of on a switch.

prompt: git switch stopped with "Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten". Why did Git refuse?
hint: The two branches disagree about that file.

choices.text: The switch would replace an edit Git has no copy of
choices.why: Right. Commit or restore it, and the switch goes through.

choices.text: You cannot switch branch with any uncommitted change
choices.why: The edit to style.css travelled fine. Only a conflicting file stops it.

choices.text: The other branch is protected
choices.why: Nothing is protected here. The message names the file that would be lost.

choices.text: index.html is not tracked on the other branch
choices.why: It is tracked on both, with different content, which is the problem.

prompt: To create a branch called menu-prices and move onto it in one step: git switch ___ menu-prices
When does git merge do a fast-forward?
hint: Can the branch you are on simply slide forward?

choices.text: When the other branch has only one commit
choices.why: The number does not matter; what matters is whether your branch moved.

choices.text: When the two branches changed different files
choices.why: That lets Git combine them without a conflict, in a merge commit. It is not a fast-forward.

choices.text: When you use --no-ff
choices.why: --no-ff is the option that forbids a fast-forward.

choices.text: When your branch has not moved since
choices.why: Right. It has no commits of its own since the other began. Then pointing it at the other branch's commit is the whole merge.

prompt: git cat-file -p on a merge commit shows two parent lines. Why two?

choices.text: One per branch it joined
choices.why: Right. The tip of main and the tip of menu-prices.

choices.text: One for the author and one for the committer
choices.why: Those are the author and committer lines, below the parents.

choices.text: Git keeps a backup of the previous commit
choices.why: Parents are how history is linked, not backups.

choices.text: The merge was done twice
choices.why: One merge, one commit, two parents.

prompt: git log --graph drew two commits side by side, both growing from 9677eef. Why could git merge not fast-forward here?
hint: Would moving main forward keep both commits?

choices.text: Neither side contains the other
choices.why: Right. No pointer can cover both. Only a new commit with two parents can.

choices.text: The two commits changed the same file
choices.why: They changed different files, and Git still needed a merge commit.

choices.text: Fast-forward is only for branches made the same day
choices.why: Time plays no part. The shape of the history decides.

choices.text: --graph turns fast-forwards off
choices.why: --graph only draws. It changes nothing.

prompt: Ana is on main and runs git merge menu-prices. Which branch moves?
hint: merge brings a branch into the one you are on.

choices.text: menu-prices
choices.why: The named branch is the one brought in; it stays where it was.

choices.text: main
choices.why: Right. menu-prices is unchanged, and can be deleted once merged.

choices.text: Both, to the merge commit
choices.why: Only the branch HEAD names moves.

choices.text: Neither; merge only prints what would change
choices.why: merge commits for real.

choices.text: Branches whose commits are all in the one you are on
choices.why: Right. Deleting their names loses nothing.

choices.text: Branches that were merged into another at least once
choices.why: It checks against the branch you are on now, not any merge ever.

choices.text: Branches that Git has deleted already
choices.why: A deleted branch is not listed anywhere.

choices.text: Branches with no commits yet
choices.why: Every branch points at a commit.

prompt: Match each command to what it does.

pairs.right: Deletes the name only if its commits are merged
Deletes the name whatever it points at
Lists branches with each one's commit

right_distractors: Deletes the branch's commits from the repository

prompt: Ana deletes experiment with -D. Git prints Deleted branch experiment (was 0704fcd). Where is Try purple now?
hint: Deleting a branch deletes a name.

choices.text: Gone from the repository, with the branch
choices.why: The commit was not deleted. Only the name was.

choices.text: Moved onto main
choices.why: -D moves nothing onto anything.

choices.text: In the repository on no branch, reachable by its id
choices.why: Right. The reflog still names it, and git switch -c experiment 0704fcd brings it back.

choices.text: In the staging area, waiting to be committed again
choices.why: It is a commit already; nothing was put in the staging area.

prompt: Ana is on experiment and runs git branch -d experiment. What happens?

choices.text: It is deleted, and she is moved to main
choices.why: Git moves nobody anywhere on its own.

choices.text: Git refuses: she has to switch away first
choices.why: Right. HEAD would name nothing.

choices.text: It is deleted along with its uncommitted changes
choices.why: It is not deleted at all.

choices.text: It is renamed instead
choices.why: Renaming is git branch -m, and it was not asked for.

prompt: Put the life of one branch in order.
items: Commit the new price on it
trap: merge brings a branch into the one you are on, so switch to main before merging.

prompt: Which of these are true? Choose all that apply.
hint: Two of them are the copy picture.

choices.text: Making a branch copies the project's files
choices.why: It writes one 41-byte file.

choices.text: A commit moves only the branch HEAD names
choices.why: Yes. That is how two branches drift apart.

choices.text: Deleting a merged branch loses none of its commits
choices.why: Yes. They are in the branch it was merged into.

choices.text: A merge commit has two parents
choices.why: Yes. One for each side it joins.

choices.text: Each branch keeps its own copy of the commits it shares
choices.why: Commits exist once and branches point into them.

prompt: A colleague says: "I made a branch, so my changes are safe from main." They have not committed anything yet. What is wrong with that?
hint: Where does an uncommitted change live?

choices.text: Nothing; a branch isolates changes from the moment it exists
choices.why: It isolates commits. The changes are still in the working tree, which every branch shares.

choices.text: Uncommitted changes follow them onto any branch
choices.why: Right. Until they are committed on the branch, they belong to no branch at all.

choices.text: Branches cannot be made while there are uncommitted changes
choices.why: They can, and the changes come along.

choices.text: main will receive the changes automatically
choices.why: Nothing reaches main except by a commit on it or a merge into it.
